# lucidity_scaling_policy (Resource)

A Lucidity autoscaler scaling policy: the buffer and size limits Lucidity applies to the disks of the instances it's attached to. Attach it to instances with lucidity_scaling_policy_attachment. All settings are updatable in place.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "lucidity_scaling_policy" "db" {
  name                      = "prod-db-volumes"
  min_buffer_in_gb          = 30
  max_buffer_in_gb          = 300
  ideal_utilization_percent = 80
  max_fs_size_in_gb         = 2000
  min_disk_sku_size         = 8
  max_disk_sku_size         = 64
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `ideal_utilization_percent` (Number) Target disk utilization, 1 to 100 percent.
- `max_buffer_in_gb` (Number) Maximum free space (buffer) to keep, in GB.
- `max_disk_sku_size` (Number) Maximum disk SKU size.
- `max_fs_size_in_gb` (Number) Maximum file system size, in GB.
- `min_buffer_in_gb` (Number) Minimum free space (buffer) to keep, in GB.
- `min_disk_sku_size` (Number) Minimum disk SKU size.
- `name` (String) Policy name. Must be unique within the Lucidity account.

### Read-Only

- `attached_instance_count` (Number) How many instances the policy is attached to. Lucidity reports only the count, not which instances.
- `id` (String) Lucidity's numeric ID for the policy. Also the import ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import ID is the policy's numeric ID.
terraform import lucidity_scaling_policy.db 33
```
